parts.title: De Ezechiéle Prophéta

verses.text: Et tu fili hóminis, sume tibi láterem, et pones eum coram te, et descríbes in eo civitátem Jerúsalem.
Et ordinábis advérsus eam obsidiónem, et ædificábis munitiónes, et comportábis ággerem, et dabis contra eam castra, et pones aríetes in gyro.
Et tu sume tibi sartáginem férream, et pones eam in murum férreum inter te et inter civitátem: et obfirmábis fáciem tuam ad eam, et erit in obsidiónem, et circúmdabis eam: signum est dómui Israël.

paragraphs: Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

Matins · Thursday, 5 November 2026

St. Martin de Porres, Conf., O.P.

St. Martin de Porres, Conf., O.P. · Duplex

Read in Latin and English

Lesson I

De Ezechiéle Prophéta

Ezek 4:1-3

Et tu fili hóminis, sume tibi láterem, et pones eum coram te, et descríbes in eo civitátem Jerúsalem. Et ordinábis advérsus eam obsidiónem, et ædificábis munitiónes, et comportábis ággerem, et dabis contra eam castra, et pones aríetes in gyro. Et tu sume tibi sartáginem férream, et pones eam in murum férreum inter te et inter civitátem: et obfirmábis fáciem tuam ad eam, et erit in obsidiónem, et circúmdabis eam: signum est dómui Israël.

Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

$Deo gratias

℟. I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and the whole earth was full of His glory; * And His train filled the temple.

℣. Above it stood the Seraphim each one had six wings.

℟. And His train filled the temple.

Lesson II

Ezek 4:6-8

Et tu dórmies super latus tuum sinístrum, et pones iniquitátes domus Israël super eo, número diérum quibus dórmies super illud: et assúmes iniquitátem eórum. Ego autem dedi tibi annos iniquitátis eórum, número diérum trecéntos et nonagínta dies: et portábis iniquitátem domus Israël. Et cum compléveris hæc, dórmies super latus tuum déxterum secúndo, et assúmes iniquitátem domus Juda quadragínta diébus: diem pro anno, diem, inquam, pro anno dedi tibi. Et ad obsidiónem Jerúsalem convértes fáciem tuam, et bráchium tuum erit exténtum: et prophetábis advérsus eam. Ecce circúmdedi te vínculis: et non te convértes a látere tuo in latus áliud, donec cómpleas dies obsidiónis tuæ.

Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

$Deo gratias

Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

$Deo gratias

℟. Look down, O Lord, from the dwelling-place of thine holiness, and take thought for us. O my God, incline thine ear, and hear. * Open thine eyes, and behold our desolation.

℣. Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, Thou That leadest Joseph like a flock.

℟. Open thine eyes, and behold our desolation.

Lesson III

From the Sermons of St. John Chrysostom, Patriarch (of Constantinople.)

On St Philogonius, Tom. iii.

The blessed N., whose Feast we are this day keeping, doth justly call on our tongue to tell what great deeds he wrought. To-day did that blessed servant of God pass into that higher life, which is a life of peace, a life where there is no trouble. To-day his ship reached that harbour whereafter wreck is to be dreaded no more. He hath felt trouble and anguish of spirit for the last time. And wherefore marvel we that that place is one where the mind is vexed no more, when we remember that Paul saith, even to men living here in this life: Rejoice evermore, pray without ceasing? (1 Thess. v. 16, 17.)

℟. Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning; * And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding.

℣. Watch therefore, for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.

℟. And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. When he will return from the wedding.

Te Deum

Read in Latin and English

Dominican Breviary, 1962. Texts from Divinum Officium (divinumofficium.com).
